lesson.title: List Positions and Updates
lesson.driving_question: How can a program use a position to read or replace one list item?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Reading and replacing list items by zero-based position
lesson.concept_budget: Read one list item and replace one list item using a valid zero-based position; bounds validation is deferred.
misconceptions: Indexing reads one item rather than the whole list.
Index assignment replaces an existing item.
The supplied position must exist in the list.
lesson.progression_note: Extends the existing introductory list lesson from whole-list operations to direct position-based access.

shared_program.filename: List Positions and Updates - Starter Code.py
shared_program.code:
supplies = ["pencil", "book", "tape"]
position = int(input("Position 0 to 2: "))
print("Old item:", supplies[position])
replacement = input("Replacement item: ")
supplies[position] = replacement
print("Updated list:", supplies)

primm.prompt: Recall the positions of three list items and how int() converts a whole-number response.
Use position 1 and replacement folder. Trace the selected old item and every item in the updated list.
Run with 1 and folder, then with 0 and pen. Confirm which position changes in each run.

questions: Why is the first list position 0 rather than 1?
What happens if the user enters position 3 for a list containing three items?
Why must the position input be converted with int() before it is used inside square brackets?
How does index assignment change one item without changing the length of the list?

primm.prompt: Replace the item at position 2 with scissors. The final list must display pencil, book and scissors in that order.
After the replacement, ask for a second valid position and display the item currently stored there. For 1/folder then 1, the selected item must be folder.
Build a three-stop route editor. Start with three place names, ask which valid position to change and the new place, then display the first stop and the complete updated route.
Repair the valid index and use square brackets for both reading and replacement.
